source.publication: 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions (with the 2025 AR1000F return)
source.section: AR1000F lines 7A-7C, 8-25, 27-29, 34, 37-38 (Form pages 1-2); Instructions PDF page 12 LINE 7A (29 per taxpayer and spouse; 65 or over on January 1, 2026; 65 Special), PDF page 14 Standard Deduction table and LINES 26-29, PDF pages 30-34 Regular Income Tax Table (schedule 0% to 5,600, 2% to 11,200, 3% to 15,990, 3.4% to 26,400, 3.9% above, as settled in the record from the table), PDF page 11 item 8 (Social Security and Railroad Retirement exempt); PDF page 11 items 12 and 13 and the NOTE (total exemptions from all plans under 12 and 13 cannot exceed 6,000 per taxpayer); PDF page 13 LINE 18A and 18B (public or private employment-related plans, the recipient does not have to be retired; traditional IRA after 59 1/2); record ar_employer_plan_exclusion, ar_traditional_ira_exclusion_59_5; Subject 206 page 1 ('You are under 59 1/2', settled against it)

worked: Single, 50: private employer pension 4,000 (for example a disability retirement). The 2025 instructions give the 6,000 for employer plans at any age ("The recipient does not have to be retired", PDF page 13); Subject 206 (2023) would deny it under 59 1/2 (approximations). Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (primary) 40,000.00 + private pension (primary) 4,000.00 = 44,000.00. Federal taxable income = 44,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 28,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). AR1000F, filing status 1 (single); Arkansas builds its own income from lines 8-25, which here equals federal AGI less the exempt items. Line 8 wages 40,000.00. Line 18A (primary, age 50): gross pension 4,000.00 = 4,000.00; less the 6,000 exemption: exemption = lesser of 4,000.00 and 6,000.00 = 4,000.00; taxable 0.00. Line 23 total income = 40,000.00; line 24 adjustments 0.00; line 25 AGI = 40,000.00. Projection check: federal AGI 44,000.00 - 6,000 exclusion (ar_retirement_exclusion_employer_plan) 4,000.00 = state AGI 40,000.00. Line 27 standard deduction (filing status 1) 2,470.00; line 28 net taxable income = 40,000.00 - 2,470.00 = 37,530.00. Line 29 tax, schedule as numbers (0% to 5,600): 2% x (11,200.00 - 5,600.00) 5,600.00 = 112.00 + 3% x (15,990.00 - 11,200.00) 4,790.00 = 143.70 + 3.4% x (26,400.00 - 15,990.00) 10,410.00 = 353.94 + 3.9% x (37,530.00 - 26,400.00) 11,130.00 = 434.07; total 1,043.71. (The Regular Income Tax Table row 37,501-37,601 gives 1,045; expected keeps the schedule.) Line 7A boxes: personal 1 = 1 x 29.00 = 29.00; line 7C and line 34 29.00; line 37 total credits 29.00. Line 38 net tax = 1,043.71 - 29.00 = 1,014.71.
accepted_approximations: Arkansas builds its own income (AR1000F lines 8 to 25) instead of starting from federal AGI; the projection starts from federal AGI less taxable Social Security (exempt) and the reliefs here.

The schedule's bracket starts are derived from the printed tax table, which rounds the tax at each row's midpoint to the dollar; between rows and in rounding the projection's tax differs from the table.

The employer-plan exclusion is given at any age, following the 2025 instructions ('The recipient does not have to be retired'). Subject 206 (revised 2/24/2023) says a person under 59 1/2 cannot qualify for the 6,000 exemption; if that applies to employer plans, people under 59.5 get no exclusion.
